docs.text: Bands of intense lake effect snow are expected tonight into Monday near many of the Great Lakes areas highlighted in this image. Dangerous to impossible travel conditions are possible, including during the Monday Morning commutes for some. Get details for your area at weather.gov

Heavy lake effect snow bands will linger east of the Great Lakes Wednesday and Thursday. A weak atmospheric river will bring periods of gusty winds, rain, and mountain snow to the Pacific Northwest through the rest of this week. Extreme cold persists over the Midwest through the Northeast U.S.
Another round of lake-effect snows is on the way Wednesday night into Thursday, with near-blizzard conditions and up to a foot of additional snow for some in the Great Lakes and Northeast regions.

An update from the NWS on the potential snow event. Read it. One key: “…As a result, the expectation is for the lake effect snow bands to be unusually intense with peak snow rates of 3 to locally 5 inches per hour, frequent lightning and thunder, and pockets of hail.” #ILwx #Chicago #ChicagoWX

Lake effect snow will continue through Friday bringing significant snowfall to areas east to southeast of the Great Lakes. Additional snowfall totals of 1 to 2 feet is forecast, with locally higher amounts of 3 feet or more possible within the heaviest snow bands over the next couple of days.

Today: Heavy lake-effect and lake-enhanced snow will persist downwind of the Great Lakes and produce some whiteout conditions that could cause difficult travel conditions, while a coastal low will produce moderate to heavy snow over parts of New England into the afternoon. weather.gov

Snow squalls may result in hazardous driving conditions across the Great Lakes, Ohio Valley, and Northeast on New Year's Eve (tomorrow) during the evening and overnight hours. This is in addition to heavy lake effect snow and light snow throughout the region over the next few days.

Lake effect snow showers will continue through Saturday downwind of Lakes Erie, Ontario & eastern portions of Lake Superior. A series of storm systems will continue to impact CA and the PacNW through the weekend into next week, bringing widespread rain, mountain snow, and gusty winds.

Heads up for winter weather tomorrow (Sunday) night into Monday. Lake effect snow bands are very hard to pinpoint, but the ingredients for a big snow event seem to exist. As usual with winter weather, the question is whetehr or not all those ingredients mix together the right way. #ILwx #ChicagoWX

Increasing confidence for heavy lake-effect snow Friday into the weekend. Cluster analysis shows us there is good agreement amongst ensembles for a 500-hPa low parked near Hudson Bay. This is a key signal for prolonged cold, westerly flow over the Great Lakes #nywx

Weather word of the week: lake effect snow. Lake effect snow occurs when cold air moves across the comparatively warmer open waters of the Great Lakes. Warmth and moisture rise, and clouds form and grow into bands that produce 2-3” of snow per hour or more. #Weather #Wx #Winter #Snow

( #NWS #GrandRapids ): The #WARM Great Lakes and #COLD #atmosphere teamed up for a week after #Thanksgiving to deliver heaps of Lake Effect #Snow. New snow measured daily amounted to over 4 FEET in parts of Northern #Michigan ( #MIwx ) . Some places saw 1 to 2 FEET of snow fall in a day #wx #wxsky
